This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur (henceforth NC: 2023:KHC-K:5441 referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.62/2016, vide its judgment and award dated 17.03.2017.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimants are the dependant legal heirs of the deceased - Yankappa, who died in a road traffic accident on 14.11.2015 when a lorry bearing registration No.AP-21/V-7194 (for short 'offending vehicle') dashed against the moped ridden by him bearing registration No.KA-36/Y-4966.
The claimants claimed that the deceased suffered injuries and was shifted to GPV Hospital, Raichur and thereafter to RIMS Hospital at Raichur from where he was shifted VIMS Hospital, Bellary.
After his treatment and discharge, he succumbed to the injuries on 26.11.2015.

The claimants claimed that Jambalamma And Ors vs Zaheer Pasha @ Jiya And Ors on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60048542/
2 the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month from business and claimed that due to the death of Sri Yankappa, they had lost financial and emotional support of the deceased and hence,
filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming NC:
2023:KHC-K:5441 compensation of Rs.26,20,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The owner of the offending vehicle contested the claim petition and denied the averments contained therein.
He contended that the claimants being the children attained majority, were not dependents on the deceased.
He also alleged that due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself, the accident was caused.
He contended that the deceased did not possess a driving licence and did not know to drive a moped.

The insurer also denied the averments of the claim petition and contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence and thereby the owner had violated conditions of policy of insurance in allowing an unauthorized person to drive the offending vehicle.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and she marked Exs.P1 to P12.
She also examined a doctor as PW.2 who treated the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5441 deceased.
The owner/insurer of offending vehicle did not lead any evidence, but marked Exs.R1 to R3 by consent.

5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle as well as the deceased had contributed to the accident, inasmuch as, the deceased did not possess a driving licence and therefore, he did not know to drive a moped and thus he had contributed 25% negligence to the cause of accident.

It considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and though there were four dependents, the Tribunal had deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:

. Particulars Amount  (in Rs.)

 2 Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/-
 3 Loss of consortium 1,00,000/-
 4 Treatment expenditure 22,000/-
 5 Loss of estate 25,000/-
 5 Transportation of dead body and 25,000/-
 funeral expenses

The Tribunal directed the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle to pay 75% of the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the Jambalamma And Ors vs Zaheer Pasha @ Jiya And Ors on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60048542/
3 date of realisation.

sentences.text: 7. Being aggrieved by the finding regarding negligence as well as quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants are in appeal.
8. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the notional income of the deceased ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
He contended that since the dependents are more than three, the Tribunal must have deducted 1/4th towards personal and living expenses rather than 1/3rd.

He also contended that the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was negligent, as he did not possess a licence, was wholly incorrect as neither the owner nor the insurer of the offending vehicle led any evidence to establish the negligence on the part of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5441 deceased.
He therefore contended that the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal deserves to be modified.
9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased by the Tribunal was just and proper.
He also contended that the deceased did not know to drive a moped and therefore, the deceased had contributed 25% negligence to the accident.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as learned counsel for the insurer.
11. The accident involving the two vehicles is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the deceased suffered injuries and thereafter succumbed to the injuries.
Neither the insurer nor the owner led any evidence to prove the negligence on the part of the deceased.

Having regard to the fact that the offending vehicle occupied a NC: 2023:KHC-K:5441 larger space on the road, unless there was evidence on record to establish the negligence on the part of the deceased, it has to be construed that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased had contributed to the accident has no basis and thus deserves to be set aside.

12. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the notional income of the deceased must have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and 1/4th of the same must have been deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The claimants are also entitled to loss of future prospects at 10%.

13. Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-

Particulars

Amount Sl.No. (in Rs.) 1 Towards loss of dependency 7,12,800/-
(Rs.8,000x1/4thx10%x12x9) 2 Medical expenses 22,000/-

Towards loss of estate 30,000/-
Total 8,04,800/-
14.

In view of the finding recorded above that the deceased was not negligent, the insurer of the offending vehicle was liable to pay the entire compensation as determined above along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
15. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.7,04,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.8,04,800/-, which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

16. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5441 Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this Judgment.
17.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant No.1 in any nationalized Bank for a period of five years.
